sentences.zh: 在太空中走过七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受特惠，网址 nytimes.com 斜杠 subscribe。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗，来自《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, after a closely watched vote, driverless cars, once a Silicon Valley fantasy, have become a 24-hour-a-day reality in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 今天，在一场备受瞩目的投票之后，曾经只是硅谷幻想的无人驾驶汽车，已经变成了旧金山全天候的现实。

sentences.en: My colleague, Cade Metz, describes the unique challenges of coexisting with cars that drive themselves.
sentences.zh: 我的同事凯德·梅茨将为我们讲述与自动驾驶汽车共存的独特挑战。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, August 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月23日，星期三。

sentences.en: Cade, we have invited you into our studio here in New York to tell us about what's happening in San Francisco, which doesn't sound very efficient, but be that as it may,
sentences.zh: 凯德，我们邀请你来到我们在纽约的演播室，给我们讲讲旧金山正在发生的事情，听起来效率不是很高，但不管怎么说，

sentences.en: San Francisco has become the capital of this grand experiment of driverless cars.
sentences.zh: 旧金山已经成为了这场宏大的无人驾驶汽车实验之都。

sentences.en: And I want you to just describe what it's like to live in San Francisco in that new reality.
sentences.zh: 我想请你描述一下在那种新现实下生活在旧金山是什么感觉。

sentences.en: As you walk through the streets, there are hundreds of these cars driving around almost constantly in most of the city.
sentences.zh: 当你走在街上，这座城市的绝大部分地方几乎随时都有数百辆这样的汽车在四处行驶。

sentences.en: Once you get out of the downtown area, the financial district, you cannot walk a block without seeing one of these cars.
sentences.zh: 一旦你离开市中心和金融区，你走不到一个街区就能看到一辆这样的汽车。

sentences.en: And if you're a first-timer in San Francisco or you've arrived for the first time in years, you cannot believe what you're seeing.
sentences.zh: 如果你是第一次来旧金山，或者多年来第一次抵达这里，你会对眼前的景象感到难以置信。

sentences.en: Hundreds of cars driving around with no one in the driver's seat.
sentences.zh: 数百辆汽车在路上行驶，而驾驶座上却空无一人。

sentences.en: These cars are not hard to spot.
sentences.zh: 这些车并不难认。

sentences.en: They're outfitted with all sorts of sensors designed to detect everything that's going on in the world around them.
sentences.zh: 它们配备了各种各样的传感器，旨在探测周围世界发生的一切。

sentences.en: These are big, sometimes trashcan-sized sensors that spin.
sentences.zh: 这些传感器体型庞大，有时像垃圾桶一样大，而且会旋转。

sentences.en: And you can't help.
sentences.zh: 你完全控制不住。

sentences.en: I'm getting an image of, like, some hybrid between a police car and a kid with braces.
sentences.zh: 我的脑海里浮现出一个画面，就像是警车和戴着牙套的小孩的结合体。

sentences.en: An analogy I like to make is the Ghostbusters car, the car from the original Ghostbusters 1984, which has all this stuff all over it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢做的一个比喻是《捉鬼敢死队》里的车，就是1984年第一部《捉鬼敢死队》里的那辆车，上面挂满了各种各样的设备。

sentences.en: Okay, so you've been in these cars.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以你坐过这些车。

sentences.en: I want you to just describe the whole experience of getting in the car and how you even get one of these driverless cars,
sentences.zh: 我想请你描述一下上车的整个体验，以及你到底是怎么叫到一辆无人驾驶汽车的，

sentences.en: because obviously it's not just a regular old, like, hail system.
sentences.zh: 因为显然它不只是那种老式的叫车系统。

sentences.en: Let's go to my most recent drive, which was last Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到我最近的一次乘车经历，就在上周三。

sentences.en: I pulled open my Waymo app where I can hail a car, much as you would an Uber.
sentences.zh: 我打开Waymo应用叫了一辆车，就像你用优步一样。

sentences.en: The difference was it wouldn't pick me up exactly where I wanted it to pick me up.
sentences.zh: 不同之处在于，它不会精确地在我想要的上车地点接我。

sentences.en: It gave me a spot in an alleyway about a block and a half away where there's less traffic.
sentences.zh: 它给我指定了一个大约一个半街区外、交通较少的小巷里的地点。

sentences.en: And eventually, my car pulls up.
sentences.zh: 最终，我的车开了过来。

sentences.en: I pull the app out again, and there's a little button on the app that says unlock.
sentences.zh: 我又打开应用，应用上有一个写着“解锁”的小按钮。

sentences.en: Good to see you, Cade.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你，凯德。

sentences.en: As I step into a car, a disembodied voice comes over the speaker that welcomes me by name.
sentences.zh: 当我坐进车里时，扬声器里传出一个没有实体的人声，用我的名字欢迎我。

sentences.en: Hello, Cade.
sentences.zh: 你好，凯德。

sentences.en: As we get going, just give us one minute to cover a few riding tips.
sentences.zh: 在我们出发之前，请花一分钟了解几个乘车小贴士。

sentences.en: It also gives me a short safety briefing.
sentences.zh: 它还向我做了一个简短的安全须知。

sentences.en: We'll do all the driving, so please don't touch the steering wheel or pedals during your ride.
sentences.zh: 我们会负责所有驾驶，所以在乘车过程中请不要触碰方向盘或踏板。

sentences.en: Then the wheel starts to turn on its own.
sentences.zh: 接着方向盘开始自己转动。

sentences.en: The car starts to move.
sentences.zh: 汽车开始移动。

sentences.en: It's like being in the car with my daughter just after she had turned 16 and was learning to drive.
sentences.zh: 这就像是和我女儿刚满16岁、正在学开车时坐在车里的感觉一样。

sentences.en: On edge.
sentences.zh: 神经紧绷。

sentences.en: Yes and no.
sentences.zh: 可以说是，也可以说不是。

sentences.en: I'm on edge because my daughter is a new driver, but also I have a daughter who is wonderfully conscientious.
sentences.zh: 我神经紧绷是因为我女儿是个新手司机，但同时我也有一个非常懂事的女儿。

sentences.en: She is so careful when she drives.
sentences.zh: 她开车时非常小心。

sentences.en: She would stop several feet before she got to the intersection.
sentences.zh: 她在到达路口前好几英尺就会停下来。

sentences.en: But that's what these driverless cars are like.
sentences.zh: 但这些无人驾驶汽车就是这个样子的。

sentences.en: They drive at the pace and with a care of a particularly conscientious 16-year-old driver.
sentences.zh: 它们的车速和谨慎程度就像是一个人格外懂事的16岁新手司机。

sentences.en: As the drive continues up and down the hills of San Francisco, it is taking much longer than it would have taken in an Uber because of that overly cautious nature of the car.
sentences.zh: 随着车子在旧金山的起伏山路间行驶，由于汽车这种过于谨慎的性格，它花的时间比坐优步要长得多。

sentences.en: You're here.
sentences.zh: 您已到达目的地。

sentences.en: Please make sure it's clear before exiting.
sentences.zh: 下车前请确保周围安全。

sentences.en: So overall, how do you rate this ride?
sentences.zh: 那么总的来说，你如何评价这次乘车体验？

sentences.en: This ghostly, driverless, cautious version of a taxi ride?
sentences.zh: 这种幽灵般、无人驾驶且谨小慎微的打车体验？

sentences.en: It got me to where I wanted to go, but it took an awful long time, relatively speaking, to get me there.
sentences.zh: 它把我送到了想去的地方，但相对而言，花的时间实在是太长了。

sentences.en: Now, the flip side, it's also like a ride at Disney World where it's a real novelty.
sentences.zh: 不过另一方面，它也挺像迪士尼乐园里的游乐设施，非常新奇。

sentences.en: It's something that you don't necessarily experience every day.
sentences.zh: 这是你平时不一定能体验到的东西。

sentences.en: And you take this ride with your senses heightened, aware of this strange thing that you're doing.
sentences.zh: 你会在感官高度兴奋的状态下体验这次乘车，意识到自己正在做一件很奇特的事情。

sentences.en: And like a lot of novelties injected into the real world like this, it is the subject of extreme debate, particularly in San Francisco where these cars have been causing accidents.
sentences.zh: 就像许多这样被引入现实世界的新奇事物一样，它引发了极大的争论，尤其是在旧金山，这些汽车一直在引发事故。

sentences.en: In some cases, those accidents cause injuries.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，这些事故造成了人员受伤。

sentences.en: They run into emergency vehicles.
sentences.zh: 它们撞上了紧急救援车辆。

sentences.en: They do things that they are not supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 它们会做出一些不该做的事情。

sentences.en: And increasingly, that is a concern for many of the residents of San Francisco who don't want their city to be a petri dish for these types of cars
sentences.zh: 而且这越来越成为许多旧金山居民的担忧，他们不希望自己的城市成为这种类型汽车的培养皿，

sentences.en: that may cause serious problems with daily life.
sentences.zh: 因为这些车可能会给日常生活带来严重的问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I'm thinking back to what you just said.
sentences.zh: 我在回想你刚才说的话。

sentences.en: It's like a ride at Disney World, but San Francisco is not Disney World.
sentences.zh: 这就像是迪士尼乐园里的游乐设施，但旧金山不是迪士尼乐园。

sentences.en: It's a city with public streets and pedestrians.
sentences.zh: 这是一座有着公共街道和行人的城市。

sentences.en: And so that makes me want to understand how we have gotten to this moment where an experiment on the scale that you are describing is even possible.
sentences.zh: 这让我很想知道，我们究竟是如何走到这一步的——让你所描述的这种规模的实验竟然成为了可能。

sentences.en: So tell us the story of how we arrive at this moment where San Francisco is filled with these ghostly driverless vehicles.
sentences.zh: 所以请给我们讲讲我们是如何走到今天这一步的，让旧金山充满了这些幽灵般的无人驾驶车辆。

sentences.en: Scientists and researchers have been trying to build autonomous vehicles since the 60s.
sentences.zh: 科学家和研究人员从20世纪60年代起就一直在尝试制造自动驾驶汽车。

sentences.en: The aim, and it is largely driven by labs funded by the Defense Department, is to build autonomous vehicles for the military.
sentences.zh: 其目标（很大程度上是由国防部资助的实验室推动的）是为军方制造自动驾驶车辆。

sentences.en: It's better to have a vehicle, a tank, that does not have a driver behind the wheel, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 最好能有一辆车，一辆坦克，可以说是没有人在驾驶座上。

sentences.en: In case it gets shot at, destroyed.
sentences.zh: 以防它遭到枪击或摧毁。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's the rough goal.
sentences.zh: 这就是大致的目标。

sentences.en: But as time goes on, people start to realize that you can do this for civilians as well, that you can use the same technology and use it to drive an ordinary car
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，人们开始意识到你也可以为平民制造这种车，你可以利用相同的技术来驾驶普通汽车，

sentences.en: and potentially change our lives as well.
sentences.zh: 并且同样有可能改变我们的生活。

sentences.en: Potentially build a car that is safer than a human being.
sentences.zh: 有可能制造出一辆比人类更安全的汽车。

sentences.en: Technology does not get tired.
sentences.zh: 技术不会感到疲劳。

sentences.en: Technology does not drink whiskey and get behind the wheel.
sentences.zh: 技术不会喝威士忌然后坐到方向盘后面。

sentences.en: There are all sorts of advantages to having technology drive as opposed to humans if you can get technology to the level where it can drive as well as we require.
sentences.zh: 如果你能把技术提升到我们所要求的驾驶水平，那么让技术代替人类驾驶有着各种各样的好处。

sentences.en: And when does that start to happen?
sentences.zh: 那这从什么时候开始发生的呢？

sentences.en: It starts to happen around 2005.
sentences.zh: 这大约从2005年开始发生。

sentences.en: DARPA, which is the research arm of the Defense Department, organizes a conteSt.
sentences.zh: 国防部的研究机构DARPA组织了一场比赛。

sentences.en: And the idea is to get all sorts of research teams to build a driverless vehicle and then compete with each other to see whose is most proficient.
sentences.zh: 其想法是让各路研究团队制造一辆无人驾驶汽车，然后互相比赛，看谁的车最熟练。

sentences.en: And two guys noticed that this is happening.
sentences.zh: 有两个人注意到了这件事。

sentences.en: They happen to be the founders of Google.
sentences.zh: 他们恰好是谷歌的创始人。

sentences.en: Larry Page and Sergey Brin.
sentences.zh: 拉里·佩奇和谢尔盖·布林。

sentences.en: One of the leaders of one of the research teams, a guy named Sebastian Thrun, tells the story of Larry Page showing up at one of these competitions in disguise,
sentences.zh: 其中一个研究团队的负责人，一个名叫塞巴斯蒂安·特伦的人，讲了一个故事：拉里·佩奇伪装后来到其中一个比赛现场，

sentences.en: a hat, sunglasses so he won't be recognized.
sentences.zh: 戴着帽子和太阳镜，以免被认出来。

sentences.en: What ends up happening is that Page hires Thrun to run a new lab at Google called Google X.
sentences.zh: 结果就是佩奇雇用了特伦在谷歌内部运营一个名为“谷歌X”的新实验室。

sentences.en: And the idea is to go after what Page and his colleagues call moonshots.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是为了追求佩奇和他的同事们所说的登月计划。

sentences.en: It's extremely ambitious technical projects.
sentences.zh: 这是极其雄心勃勃的技术项目。

sentences.en: The first thing they decide to go after is a driverless car.
sentences.zh: 他们决定涉足的第一件事就是无人驾驶汽车。

sentences.en: The ultimate moonshot.
sentences.zh: 终极登月计划。

sentences.en: The ultimate moonshot.
sentences.zh: 终极登月计划。

sentences.en: Larry Page wants to put one of these in your driveway to put you in a car on a daily basis that can drive by itself, get you to where you want to go
sentences.zh: 拉里·佩奇想把其中一辆车放到你的车道上，让你每天都能坐上一辆能够自主驾驶、把你送到你想去的地方的汽车，

sentences.en: while you're doing something else.
sentences.zh: 同时你可以做别的事情。

sentences.en: Taking a nap, reading to your kid.
sentences.zh: 小睡一会儿，或者给你的孩子读书。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And that's something that excites a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 这让很多人感到兴奋。

sentences.en: But there's an interesting difference of opinion between Thrun and Page that explains the next 10 years of development with this technology.
sentences.zh: 但在特伦和佩奇之间存在着一个有趣的意见分歧，这解释了这项技术在接下来10年的发展。

sentences.en: Larry Page, running a company like Google,
sentences.zh: 拉里·佩奇经营着像谷歌这样的公司，

sentences.en: wants to see this happen.
sentences.zh: 希望看到这一切发生。

sentences.en: Sebastian Thrun, the man he's hired to run this lab and to run this project, he realizes how difficult this will be.
sentences.zh: 塞巴斯蒂安·特伦，这个被他雇来管理这个实验室和这个项目的人，他意识到这会有多困难。

sentences.en: He realizes how far they will have to go.
sentences.zh: 他意识到他们还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: And he doesn't necessarily know how to get there.
sentences.zh: 而且他并不一定知道该如何实现。

sentences.en: And why is it such a challenge?
sentences.zh: 为什么这是一个如此巨大的挑战？

sentences.en: Why in Thrun's mind is it going to be so hard to realize Larry Page's vision of a driverless car in every driveway?
sentences.zh: 为什么在特伦看来，要实现拉里·佩奇关于“每家每户车道上都停着一辆无人驾驶汽车”的愿景会如此困难？

sentences.en: Getting a car to make a left turn at an intersection is not difficult.
sentences.zh: 让汽车在十字路口左转并不困难。

sentences.en: A right turn is not difficult.
sentences.zh: 右转也不困难。

sentences.en: Accelerating, braking, those things are not difficult.
sentences.zh: 加速、刹车，这些事情都不困难。

sentences.en: What's difficult is dealing with all the chaos that we encounter every time we get into a car.
sentences.zh: 困难的是应对我们每次上车时都会遇到的所有混乱。

sentences.en: The unexpected is likely to happen at any given second.
sentences.zh: 意想不到的事情随时都可能发生。

sentences.en: You have to have a machine that completely, first of all,
sentences.zh: 你必须拥有一台机器，首先它能完全，

sentences.en: recognize what is going on around it.
sentences.zh: 识别周围发生的事情。

sentences.en: You need to know that that is a pedestrian and not a bicycle.
sentences.zh: 你需要知道那是行人而不是自行车。

sentences.en: Then, once you are clear on everything that is around you, you need to predict what's going to happen with each of those things.
sentences.zh: 然后，一旦你弄清楚了周围的一切，你就需要预测这些事情中每一件接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: And then once you predict what's going to happen, you need to develop a way of responding to all that.
sentences.zh: 一旦你预测了将要发生的事情，你就需要开发一种应对所有这些情况的方法。

sentences.en: And that requires reason.
sentences.zh: 这就需要推理能力。

sentences.en: It requires a quality that machines still don't have and certainly didn't have in the early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 它需要一种机器仍然不具备、而且在2000年代初绝对不具备的品质。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Driving a car isn't just about steering the wheel as you go down the road.
sentences.zh: 开车不只是在路上行驶时转动方向盘。

sentences.en: It's about responding to all the possible things that could go wrong.
sentences.zh: 它是关于应对所有可能出错的潜在情况。

sentences.en: Dog runs out into the road, bike swerves into your path.
sentences.zh: 狗突然跑上马路，自行车突然拐进你的车道。

sentences.en: We, as humans, learn to respond instinctively to those.
sentences.zh: 我们人类学会了对这些情况做出本能的反应。

sentences.en: It's harder to teach a robot to do that.
sentences.zh: 教机器人这样做要困难得多。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But despite how challenging teaching a robot all that is, we know that this driverless car technology does move forward.
sentences.zh: 但尽管教机器人这一切充满挑战，我们知道这项无人驾驶汽车技术确实在向前发展。

sentences.en: So, tell us how that happened.
sentences.zh: 所以，给我们讲讲这是怎么发生的吧。

sentences.en: Larry Page, the founder of Google, says go after this, and Thrun goes after it.
sentences.zh: 谷歌创始人拉里·佩奇说去追求这个目标，特伦就去做了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Jump, how high?
sentences.zh: 要我跳多高？

sentences.en: So, in 2009,
sentences.zh: 所以在2009年，

sentences.en: And by 2010, they quietly start testing this technology on the public roads of California.

sentences.en: A secret driverless car project that puts those driverless cars on the road.

sentences.en: And in the fall of 2010, let the world know that it was happening.
sentences.zh: 并在2010年秋天让全世界知道了这件事。

sentences.en: And what is the response?

sentences.en: Well, it sets off a tech arms race.

sentences.en: Not only among dedicated technology companies like Google, but among a new type of company which is doing ride hailing,

sentences.en: And as companies like Google and Uber started to talk about this technology publicly,
sentences.zh: 正当谷歌和优步等公司开始公开谈论这项技术时，

sentences.zh: 塞巴斯蒂安·特龙（Sebastian Thrun）帮助启动了谷歌的自动驾驶汽车项目。

sentences.en: They talked about it as if it was around the corner.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论它的语气，就好像它马上就要实现了一样。

sentences.en: Will they be functional in two to three years or available in two to three years?

sentences.zh: 它们现在就已经能用了，而且将在两到三年内上市。

sentences.en: They'd be in the marketplace.

sentences.en: If you were reading the tech press, if you were reading the mainstream press around that time, ready or not, they're coming.
sentences.zh: 如果你当时阅读科技媒体，如果你阅读主流媒体，无论你准备好没有，它们都要来了。

sentences.en: You assumed that by the following year, those driverless cars we've been hearing so much about could soon be hitting the road, cruising right alongside us in the next few years.
sentences.zh: 你会以为，到了第二年，我们听说了那么多的那些无人驾驶汽车很快就会上路，在未来几年里就会和我们并肩行驶。

sentences.en: You would have a driverless car in your driveway if you wanted one.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要的话，你的车道上就会停着一辆无人驾驶汽车。

sentences.en: Nissan plans to sell a driverless car in just five years and hopes to bring the self-driving cars to the market by 2020.
sentences.zh: 日产计划在短短五年内销售无人驾驶汽车，并希望在2020年之前将自动驾驶汽车推向市场。

sentences.en: Ford hopes to have a fully autonomous vehicle available by 2021.
sentences.zh: 福特希望在2021年之前推出完全自动驾驶汽车。

sentences.en: Your driveway could disappear and so could parking lots and garages.
sentences.zh: 你家的车道可能会消失，停车场和车库也是如此。

sentences.en: Freight and packages could all move at night.
sentences.zh: 货运和包裹都可以在夜间运输。

sentences.en: And that was never the case.

sentences.en: There was some hype.

sentences.zh: 硅谷总是充满炒作。

sentences.en: In this case, the hype was particularly strong.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，炒作尤为强烈。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So now that all these big players are pumping this extraordinary amount of money into this unproven technology, what becomes of it?
sentences.zh: 既然所有这些大玩家都在向这项未经验证的技术投入巨额资金，那它最后会变成什么样呢？

sentences.en: On the surface, the types of cars being built were perfect.
sentences.zh: 从表面上看，制造出来的这些汽车堪称完美。

sentences.en: Reporters would get into a car in Mountain View, California.
sentences.zh: 记者们会坐上加利福尼亚州山景城的一辆汽车。

sentences.en: It would take them around the block.
sentences.zh: 它会载着他们绕街区行驶。

sentences.en: It was nary a mistake.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有出任何差错。

sentences.en: But the reality below the surface was that building this technology was extremely difficult.
sentences.zh: 但表面之下的现实却是，构建这项技术极其困难。

sentences.en: And that continued for years where the hype did not reflect the reality.
sentences.zh: 这种情况持续了好几年，炒作与现实并不相符。

sentences.en: But then that changed in 2018.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况在2018年改变了。

sentences.en: Which is when?

sentences.en: There was a crash in Arizona involving an Uber test car.
sentences.zh: 亚利桑那州发生了一起涉及优步测试车的车祸。

sentences.zh: 夜间，一名49岁的女性推着自行车穿过一条多车道马路。

sentences.en: She was struck and killed.
sentences.zh: 她被撞身亡。

sentences.en: There was a safety driver behind the wheel who was supposed to take over if something went wrong, but they did not.
sentences.zh: 方向盘后面有一个安全员，本应在出问题时接管车辆，但他们没有这样做。

sentences.en: The bottom line is someone was killed by a self-driving car and that almost immediately set the industry back.
sentences.zh: 最根本的是，有人死于自动驾驶汽车，这几乎立刻让整个行业倒退了。

sentences.en: Yes, people behind the wheel are involved in accidents every day.
sentences.zh: 是的，方向盘后面的司机每天都在卷入事故。

sentences.en: People die because of those accidents.
sentences.zh: 人们因为这些事故而丧生。

sentences.en: But if a new technology kills someone, that is far more concerning to the general public, to regulators, they start to wonder if this is going to work.
sentences.zh: 但如果是一项新技术害死了人，公众和监管机构就会更加担忧，他们开始怀疑这到底行不行得通。

sentences.en: After the crash,
sentences.zh: 车祸发生后，

sentences.zh: 优步立即暂停了这些车辆的测试工作，不仅在亚利桑那州，还在加利福尼亚州和匹兹堡。

sentences.en: Toyota follows suit and slowly all these companies start to admit that this is harder than they had let on.
sentences.zh: 丰田紧随其后，慢慢地，所有这些公司都开始承认，这比他们之前表现出来的要难得多。

sentences.en: Even Google starts to change the way it's doing things.
sentences.zh: 就连谷歌也开始改变其行事方式。

sentences.zh: 它的自动驾驶汽车业务被分拆成了一家名为Waymo的新公司，其雄心也开始发生转变，从“你家车道上停辆车”的愿景，转向了

sentences.en: of robo-taxi service that Uber and Lyft were building.
sentences.zh: 优步和来福车正在构建的那种机器人出租车服务。

sentences.zh: 这些公司决定不再去搞一辆可以在任何地方行驶的私家车，而是将自动驾驶汽车服务限制在某个特定的

sentences.zh: 如果你在旧金山画一个圈，把你的汽车限制在那一个城市，你就可以建立一幅数字地图，一幅该城市的逼真三维视觉地图，然后你可以把

sentences.zh: 这幅地图交个汽车，接着在这个受限的环境中进行一遍又一遍的测试。

sentences.en: You limit the chaos, you limit the unexpected moments, that's going to be easier, and that's what the industry starts to go after.
sentences.zh: 你限制了混乱，限制了意料之外的时刻，这就会变得更容易，而这正是行业开始追求的方向。

sentences.en: And that's how we get to the point where San Francisco, the second most dense city in America, becomes a testing ground for these driverless vehicles with hundreds of cars
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么旧金山——美国人口密度第二高的城市——会成为这些无人驾驶汽车的试验场，数百辆汽车

sentences.en: driving around the city.
sentences.zh: 在城市中行驶。

sentences.en: All of this comes to a head with a public hearing earlier this month in California where the future of these companies in this city will be decided.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切在本月初加利福尼亚州的一场公开听证会上达到了顶峰，会上将决定这些公司在这个城市的未来。

sentences.zh: 摆在眼前的问题是，它们能否像优步或来福车一样在这个城市运营，只是司机不在方向盘后面？
